gap: No result ChatGPT got says which battery inverters can run a SubDrive-controlled well pump. Franklin's SubDrive Connect manual sets the minimum generator at 1.5× the drive's maximum input watts: 5,700 W for a SubDrive20, so the drive draws up to about 3,800 W at 240 V. Because the drive soft-starts the motor, the inverter's continuous 240 V rating decides the pick, not its surge rating. A 3,840 W BLUETTI Apex 300 barely covers a SubDrive20, while a $1,220 Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V split-phase unit covers a SubDrive20 or SubDrive30.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. The Franklin SubDrive/MonoDrive FAQ makes no statement about generators, inverters or battery backup, and only gives a 190–260 VAC line-voltage range and an F2 fault below 180 VAC. The SubDrive Connect product page lists 1/2–5 hp, soft start and three SKUs, but no input watts, no generator sizing and no prices. The generator table sits in the uncited owner's manual results (#6, #7, #8, #13, and the same ManualsLib manual as #15, one page later), so the raw generator figure is partly available. None of the 16 results ties it to an inverter's continuous rating, and none names or prices any battery inverter. ChatGPT's own answer only said 'pure sine wave inverter with high surge capacity', which points the shopper at surge when the soft-starting SubDrive makes continuous 240 V output the limit.
decides: This changes the ranking for shoppers who already have, or are buying, ChatGPT's top pick (the Franklin SubDrive). Surge rating stops mattering, and our current page's surge column is the wrong lead spec for them. Continuous 240 V output decides instead: it must exceed about 3,800 W for a SubDrive20, about 4,670 W for a SubDrive30, and about 7,330 W for a SubDrive50. The Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V split-phase ($1,220) and SPH6548P ($1,035) clear the SubDrive20 and SubDrive30. For a SubDrive50, only the Sun Gold 8KW ($1,305) or larger units clear it. The BLUETTI Apex 300's 3,840 W has only 40 W of headroom over a SubDrive20. For a plain across-the-line well pump with no SubDrive, the surge-first ranking still holds, and the Sun Gold 6000W 48V (18,000 W for 20 s, $1,220) beats the AIMS unit with the same 18,000 W / 20 s surge by $1,028.86.

findings.label: Generator sizing rule
findings.value: 1.5 × maximum input watts consumed by the drive, rounded up to next standard generator size
findings.source_title: Franklin Electric SUBDRIVE CONNECT Owner's Manual, p. 12 (Generator Sizing)
findings.note: Quoted from the manual: 'Basic generator sizing for the SubDrive Connect system is 1.5 times the maximum input watts consumed by the drive.' The same page says 'Do not use with a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI).' The section does not mention inverters.

findings.label: Minimum generator
findings.source_title: Franklin Electric SUBDRIVE CONNECT Owner's Manual, p. 12
findings.note: The extracted table lists SubDrive15/20/30/50 against 3,500/5,700/7,000/11,000 W in order. I matched models to values by that order, and the Spanish manual on manualslib.mx gives the same sequence. Implied maximum input is 5,700 / 1.5 = 3,800 W. Since the generator figure is rounded up, the real maximum input is at most 3,800 W. Check the mapping against the printed page before publishing.

findings.label: Supply voltage
findings.value: 190–260 VAC; F2 undervoltage fault below 180 VAC L1–L2
findings.note: This means the backup source must deliver 240 V. A 120 V-only inverter or power station cannot run it. The page also says GFCI/AFCI breakers 'may cause nuisance trips'.

findings.label: Range and soft start
findings.value: 1/2–5 hp; soft start included; single-phase 2-wire, 3-wire or three-phase motors
findings.note: Soft start is why the inverter's continuous rating, not its surge rating, limits a SubDrive system. The FAQ adds that two-wire motors cannot soft start. The page lists no price.
